questions.stem: Find the derivative of xˣ.
Find the derivative of eˣ with respect to √x.
If y = ae^(nx) + be^(−nx), show that y″ = n²y.
Find the second order derivative of y = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)).
If y = x + tan x, show that cos²x · d²y/dx² + 2x = 2y.
If y = (2x + 3)/(4x + 5), find y″.
If y = log(4x² − 9), find y″.

If y = xʸ, show that dy/dx = y²/(x(1 − log y)) = y²/(x(1 − y log x)).

questions.stem: Find the derivative of tan⁻¹((3a²x − x³)/(a(a² − 3x²))).
Find dy/dx for x = a((1 − t²)/(1 + t²)), y = 2bt/(1 + t²).
If f(x) = tan⁻¹((√(1 + x²) − 1)/x) and g(x) = tan⁻¹x, differentiate f(x) with respect to g(x).
Find the derivative of tan⁻¹(sec x + tan x).
If y = a cos x + (b + 2x) sin x, show that y″ + y = 4 cos x.
If y = ax^(n+1) + bx^(−n), prove that x²y″ = n(n + 1)y.
If y = a cos(sin x) + b sin(sin x), prove that y₂ + (tan x)y₁ + y cos²x = 0.
If x = a(t − sin t) and y = a(1 + cos t), find d²y/dx².
If ay⁴ = (x + b)⁵, show that 5yy″ = (y′)².
If √(1 − x²) + √(1 − y²) = a(x − y), show that dy/dx = √((1 − y²)/(1 − x²)).
Find dy/dx if y = (sin x)ˣ + x^(sin x).

questions.notes: The stars are printed on the sub-part (***ii)).

questions.stem: If y = tan⁻¹[(√(1 + x²) + √(1 − x²))/(√(1 + x²) − √(1 − x²))] for 0 < |x| < 1, find dy/dx.
If y = x√(a² + x²) + a² log(x + √(a² + x²)), prove that dy/dx = 2√(a² + x²).
If xʸ = yˣ, show that dy/dx = y(x log y − y)/(x(y log x − x)).
If x^(log y) = log x, show that dy/dx = (y/x)[(1 − log x log y)/(log x)²].
If xʸ + yˣ = aᵇ, show that dy/dx = −[(yx^(y−1) + yˣ log y)/(xʸ log x + xy^(x−1))].
If f(x) = sin⁻¹√((x − β)/(α − β)) and g(x) = tan⁻¹√((x − β)/(α − x)), show that f′(x) = g′(x), where β < x < α.
questions.notes: The printed g(x) radicand runs into the page edge on scan 72; read as (x − β)/(α − x).

questions.stem: If y = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)) + tan⁻¹((3x − x³)/(1 − 3x²)) − tan⁻¹((4x − 4x³)/(1 − 6x² + x⁴)), show that dy/dx = 1/(1 + x²).
Find the derivative dy/dx of the function y = [(1 − 2x)^(2/3)(1 + 3x)^(−3/4)]/[(1 − 6x)^(5/6)(1 + 7x)^(−6/7)].
Find the derivative of f(x) = tan⁻¹(2x/(1 − x²)) with respect to g(x) = sin⁻¹(2x/(1 + x²)).
If a > b > 0 and 0 < x < π, and f(x) = (a² − b²)^(−1/2) cos⁻¹((a cos x + b)/(a + b cos x)), show that f′(x) = 1/(a + b cos x).
